value.note: TI ships two silicon revisions under one datasheet and specifies them separately throughout — this is a genuine second premise, not a source disagreement. With the revision undeclared, on_unknown='strictest' takes the new chip's higher 2.5 V floor so a 2.3 V design is not silently blessed. Note the very wide 16 V ceiling: this part tolerates a 12 V input where the AP2112 (6 V) cannot.

value.note: Fixed-output part available in 100 mV steps across the range shown, so this slot records the AVAILABLE OPTION RANGE rather than one device's output. The two revisions differ: the legacy chip reaches 10 V, the new chip only 5.0 V — so a 6 V LP2985 exists only as legacy silicon. Output accuracy is +/-0.5% on the new chip, +/-1% for legacy A-grade and +/-1.5% for legacy standard grade.

value.note: Dropout depends on BOTH load current and silicon revision, so each arm carries two conditions. The values below are the datasheet's OVER-TEMPERATURE maxima (-40 to 125 degC), which is the figure a rail-feasibility check should use; the 25 degC typicals are much lower (legacy 7/40/120/280 mV and new 11.5/98/120/180 mV at 1/10/50/150 mA). Load bands overlap at their edges and are combined with max_of_matching so the worse figure wins. At no load the maxima are 5 mV (legacy) and 3 mV (new). The revisions diverge sharply at full load: 575 mV for legacy versus 254 mV for the new chip, so a 3.3 V output from a 3.6 V Li-ion input is viable on new silicon and marginal on legacy. TI defines VDO as the input-to-output differential at which the output falls 100 mV below its value at a 1 V differential (footnote 1, p.7).

value.note: Continuous output current, stated as a range 0 to 150 mA in the Recommended Operating Conditions and as 'Output current: Up to 150mA' in the features. Short-circuit output current is separately given as 400 mA for the legacy chip and 375 mA for the new chip. NOTE for regulator-adequacy checks: 150 mA is NOT enough for an ESP32, which needs at least 500 mA (ESP32 datasheet Table 5-2 IVDD) — this part suits sensor and MCU rails, not a Wi-Fi SoC.

value.note: The two revisions have materially different stability requirements: the legacy chip wants 2.2 to 4.7 uF, while the new chip accepts 1 to 200 uF with 2.2 uF nominal and is advertised as 'Stable with 2.2 uF ceramic capacitors'. With the revision unknown the strictest 2.2 uF floor applies. Three qualifications from the same table: (a) footnote 1 — capacitors derate to 50% of nominal, and an EFFECTIVE output capacitance of 1 uF minimum must be maintained for stability; (b) footnote 3 — maximum supported ESR on the new chip is 1 ohm, and for a higher-ESR output capacitor a low-ESR 100 nF MLCC must be placed close to the output pin; (c) legacy-chip ESR guidance lives in a separate 'Recommended Capacitors for the Legacy Chip' section.

value.note: 10 nF on the BYPASS pin. This is the capacitor the part's headline noise specification is measured with: 'Low noise: 30 uVRMS with 10nF bypass capacitor', and the Electrical Characteristics output-noise row states its conditions as CBYPASS = 10 nF, COUT = 2.2 uF, VOUT = 3.3 V, ILOAD = 150 mA. Ripple rejection is likewise specified at CBYPASS = 10 nF (78 dB new chip, 45 dB legacy at 1 kHz). Omitting it does not stop the regulator working but forfeits the low-noise behaviour that is the reason to choose this part. The Recommended Operating Conditions also give VBYPASS as 1.2 V. It appears in the datasheet's own Typical Application Circuit on p.1.
